# Lanesra OS

Lanesra OS is a free, open-source, self-hostable, AI-native business application platform for small and mid-size organizations. It leads with an AI Agent Foundry and Unified AI Gateway where named AI agents run directly against your real data, not a bolted-on chatbot with a separate context pipeline, and a native MCP server & CLI that expose that same data to Claude Desktop, an IDE agent or any MCP-capable client. Both sit on the same no-code platform for building whatever a business actually needs, which also powers a complete CRM out of the box — your Business OS — and an Industry Data Model of 11 ready-made industry apps to install instead of building from scratch. Deployment Management packages and promotes customizations across environments, and an Integration Hub connects it to every other system a business already runs.

## What it is, in eight layers

1. **AI Agent Foundry** — a Unified AI Gateway (bring your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible/Google Gemini key, or route to a fully local/air-gapped model via Ollama, with automatic failover and per-agent/per-workspace token budgets), named agents with a persona, a per-tool Actions checklist, persistent Memory, a shared Skills library, and delegation, Orchestration (deterministic Pipelines, schedule/webhook/workflow-fired runs), a conversational Chat Assistant with real tool access, and a Context Layer with ranked full-text search and embeddings-based Vector Search over records — every agent runs directly against the same Core CRM/Custom Object data model below, no separate context pipeline. Every agent also carries a real Draft → Test → Published → Deprecated → Disabled version lifecycle (a Published version is an immutable snapshot, optionally declaring a Structured Output JSON-schema contract validated with one repair retry), and a durable, workspace-wide Approval Service generalizes "something needs a human decision" beyond a single Pipeline step. AI Agent Platform v2 adds four more layers on top: a Policy Engine & Tool-Call Firewall (six-tier tool risk classification, a workspace/per-agent approval threshold and blocklist, formalized into the exact schema→permission→policy→approval→execute→audit dispatch every tool call already ran through); a shared, durable, checkpointed Execution Graph Runtime (12 node types) now underlying every Workflow and Pipeline, with a free-form drag-and-drop **Agent Teams** canvas to author one directly; typed Memory Architecture (Session/Working/Entity memory alongside the Agent Memory document above, each scoped/TTL'd/Policy-gated) and Document RAG (chunked, embedded Knowledge Sources a `search_knowledge` call always cites); and an MCP client role (next item).
2. **MCP** — a native Model Context Protocol server (`POST /mcp`, JSON-RPC 2.0) exposing that same data and business logic to Claude Desktop, an IDE agent, or any MCP-capable client, plus a companion CLI giving humans and shell scripts the same REST API access without an agent in the loop — both authenticated with the same scoped API keys the REST API already uses. The same protocol now runs in reverse too: an MCP client role lets a workspace connect an external MCP server as a Connection, discover its tools via real `initialize`/`tools/list` JSON-RPC calls, and opt them in as agent-callable tools through the identical Tool-Call Firewall above (read-only by default, a two-level write gate for anything destructive).
3. **No-code platform primitives** — Custom Objects (entirely new record types, no code), Custom Relationships (any two record types, any cardinality, including self-referential hierarchies and a polymorphic "any type" target), Screen/App Builder (named layouts by role, Draft → Publish), Business Rules (multi-condition AND/OR, 10 operators, including a condition that reads a related record's field through a relationship) and Workflow Automation (7 trigger types, 8+ action types, including a date-reached trigger on any custom object's own date field), custom Dashboards and Reports (with an "as of" effective-dating filter). An Administrator reshapes the workspace from a settings screen — no developer required. Both the AI Agent Foundry above and the Core CRM below are built on this same layer.
4. **Organization & Access Control** — an Organization Unit hierarchy (materialized-path, so a subtree move is one bounded update) under one Organization per workspace, Work Teams with time-bounded memberships (ending one never reassigns anything the member owned), and a structured Owner (user or team) plus Owning Organization Unit on every Core CRM and Custom Object record, with bulk reassignment and a full ownership-transfer history. Access Control v1 layers capability-scoped Access Roles (per-object create/read/update/delete/assign) and a Record Scope (Owner-only, Owner's Team, Owner's Org Unit and below, or Organization-wide) on top, enforced on every single-record and list/search/dashboard/report view, with an Access Inspector explaining why a user can or can't see a given record. Field Access Policies, AI Action Levels and Enterprise Identity/SSO are roadmapped next.
5. **Core CRM** — Companies, Contacts, Opportunities, Products, Quotes, Orders, Invoices, Contracts and Tasks, connected in one flexible sales lifecycle (Company → Opportunity → Quote → Order → Invoice), with dashboards, reports and global search.
6. **Industry Data Model** — a versioned package manifest format (objects, fields, relationships, rules, workflows, screens, reports and a dashboard) installed into an existing workspace, reusing its existing Company/Contact/Task core rather than creating a parallel data model; 11 ready-made industry apps (Field Service, Property Management, Construction & Contractors, Professional Services, Practice Administration, Recruitment & Staffing, Real Estate Brokerage, Legal Practice, Nonprofit & Association Management, Auto Repair & Service Garage, Policy Administration & Claims Management) install in a few clicks, each validated, backed up and installed transactionally. A separate Lanesra Industry Foundation package (desktop only) — Party, Party Role, Party Relationship, Location, Asset, Agreement and more — is shared cross-industry plumbing other packages can optionally depend on instead of reinventing. A plain App Builder (part of the no-code layer above) still groups any hand-built set of objects into your own named, publishable app with role/user-based access.
7. **Deployment Management** — a Publisher registry with namespace validation, named/versioned Solutions (a curated subset of components), export/import between workspaces, and update-with-diff for reviewing and applying a newer package version — the same "build in test, promote to production" pattern enterprise platforms use, without enterprise licensing.
8. **Integration Hub** — encrypted Connections (REST, SFTP, PostgreSQL, OData, SMTP), OpenAPI-imported Connectors usable as Workflow Automation actions or, once an admin opts a connector in (read-only by default, write access behind a further explicit opt-in), as AI Agent Foundry tools, a generic REST API with hashed/scoped API keys, HMAC-signed outbound Webhooks with retry, a CSV data-exchange wizard, read-only External Objects, and scheduled Integration Jobs for recurring sync — desktop-only today.

## Current status

- Early Access — the desktop app itself is at v0.14.0; the website/product tracks a separate sequential version counter, now at v0.83.0
- Windows desktop edition (Tauri + Rust + SQLite): the full sales lifecycle, Contracts, Tasks, user management, Team Workspace mode for small teams (Docker), backup/restore, self-service password change, PDF generation/printing, and CSV import/export all working. desktop-v0.14.0 is the latest tagged Early Access Windows installer (.exe/.msi) on GitHub Releases (unsigned); build and run from source is also supported.
- No-code platform (desktop and demo): Custom Objects, Custom Relationships, Screen/App Builder, Business Rules, Workflow Automation, Dashboards, Reports, global search, Saved Views & Bulk Actions. Five engine-hardening additions - self-referential and polymorphic relationships, a cross-record business rule/workflow condition, a custom-object date-reached trigger, and an "as of" effective-dating report filter - are desktop only for now, not mirrored in the online demo.
- Organization & Access Control (desktop and demo): Organizations, a materialized-path Organization Unit hierarchy, Work Teams with time-bounded memberships, and a structured Owner (user or team) + Owning Organization Unit on every Core CRM and Custom Object record, with bulk reassignment and ownership-transfer history. Access Control v1 (capability-scoped Access Roles, Record Scopes, an Access Inspector) is shipped and enforced across single-record CRUD plus list/search/dashboard/report views. Field Access Policies, AI Action Levels and Enterprise Identity/SSO are roadmapped, not built yet.
- Voice-First Mode (desktop and demo, all 4 PRs of the rollout shipped): a PIN-gated, time-boxed Voice session; 8 per-Access-Role capability toggles, a Max Voice Action Level and a Processing Boundary label that only ever narrow (never widen) a role's existing object permissions; a metadata-driven planner recognizing navigate/query/create-task/create-record/capture-interaction/update-status/run-agent commands with honest entity resolution (exact match, clarifying question, or "not found" - never a silent guess); risk-classified execution (immediate reads, an explicit Before → After Confirm/Reject step for writes and agent/pipeline runs, a hard block on delete-class actions) routed through the same entity service or AI Agent Foundry/Orchestration entry point the UI and REST API already use; real Undo for a status change or created task; and a full My Voice Activity / admin Voice Activity audit trail. A RUN_AGENT intent lets a spoken command kick off a named AI Agent or Pipeline, gated by its own capability toggle and whatever admin-only restriction the target already carries. A reference like "it"/"that" now survives across a whole back-and-forth, not just the record open on screen: each session keeps its own bounded (5-turn) history of what it last resolved, consulted as a second, lower-confidence fallback behind live screen context, with a one-click reset. Entity resolution now covers every active Custom Object (including ones from an installed Industry App) identically on both platforms, and a bounded Levenshtein-based fuzzy match tier resolves a typo'd name when an exact/substring search comes back empty (still asking rather than guessing when more than one candidate is plausible). The online demo's speech synthesis is now honest about failure (utterance start/end/error events plus a safety-timeout, instead of a silent stuck state) and speaks every response, not just completed actions; its Voice-First Mode panel is a full-screen conversational overlay (ChatGPT/Siri/Gemini voice-mode style: animated orb, live transcript, hands-free auto-resuming listening between turns). A CREATE intent guides record creation one field at a time - name first, then any required custom field - for Company and any Custom Object (Contact/Opportunity/Quote/Order/Contract/Task all need a related Company chosen first, an honestly named gap, not built yet). PR 3: a spoken command now resolves against an installed Industry App's own status vocabulary (Property Management's Unit "Occupancy Status," etc.), not just the generic Active/Inactive/Archived column every Custom Object shares; Quiet Mode - previously stored but never actually checked before speaking, a real bug - now genuinely silences responses with a visible 🔇 indicator; and the stored short/normal/detailed response-detail preference now shapes real spoken phrasing (a terser or fuller variant of each plan step's description) instead of doing nothing. PR 4 closes out the rollout with an optional, admin-opt-in conversational layer: only when the deterministic planner above returns "unsupported," the transcript is sent to the workspace's own chosen `ai_providers` row via the existing Gateway with exactly one narrow job - rewrite it into a supported command phrasing, or ask a clarifying question - never to resolve a record, decide risk, or execute anything itself; the rewritten text is fed straight back into the identical planner/resolver/risk/execution pipeline a manually-phrased command already goes through, gated by the same Use AI Agents capability RUN_AGENT already uses. Real local/on-device speech recognition remains the one honestly named roadmapped gap.
- App Catalog (desktop and demo): all 11 industry reference packages install transactionally into an existing workspace.
- Lanesra Industry Foundation (desktop only): shared cross-industry objects (Party, Party Role, Party Relationship, Location, Asset, Agreement, ...) other packages can optionally declare a real, enforced dependency on and relate to - not mirrored in the online demo, which has no dependency-checking of any kind for any package.
- Deployment Management (desktop and demo): Publishers, versioned Solutions, real export/import, update-with-diff.
- Integration Hub (desktop only, real): AES-256-GCM-encrypted Connections, OpenAPI Connector import (with a curated template gallery - OpenAI, Cohere, Slack, GitHub, SendGrid - to start from instead of always pasting a spec), a generic REST API secured by hashed scoped API keys, HMAC-signed Webhooks, a CSV data-exchange wizard, External Objects, and a real background-scheduled Integration Jobs engine on the Team Workspace server. A Tool Bridge turns an opted-in connector's Actions into real AI Agent Foundry tools - read-only by default, write access behind a further explicit per-connector opt-in, and fails closed rather than exposing a tool for a Connector Action whose request-body schema can't be confidently typed. The online demo simulates the rest of this layer client-side (no server to make a real call from).
- AI & Agentic Layer (desktop and demo): a native MCP server & CLI, a Chat Assistant, the AI Agent Foundry (named agents with persona, Actions, Memory, Skills, delegation), Orchestration (Pipelines/Triggers/workflow-fired runs, with human-approval gates on any topology's own resume point), and a Unified AI Gateway (multi-provider routing, failover, token budgets, DLP air-gapping) are all shipped. A Context Layer adds ranked full-text search over Custom Object records (SQLite FTS5/`bm25()` — lexical relevance) and real change-history for every agent's Memory; Vector Search (desktop only, opt-in) adds a second, meaning-based ranking on top - real embeddings from the workspace's own already-configured OpenAI-compatible/Gemini provider, stored as plain SQLite BLOBs and compared by cosine similarity in Rust, not a bundled vector database. AI Agent Platform v2, Phase 1 adds a real Draft → Test → Published → Deprecated → Disabled version lifecycle per agent (a Published version immutable, optionally declaring a Structured Output JSON-schema contract with one repair retry), plus a durable, workspace-wide Approval Service generalizing "something needs a human decision" beyond a single Pipeline step's own pause flag - every agent-driven write is now also attributed to that agent's own identity in the audit trail, alongside the initiating user. Phase 2 adds a Tool Registry (six-tier risk classification per tool) and a unified Policy Engine (workspace/per-agent approval threshold + blocklist), formalized into a named Tool-Call Firewall on the exact dispatch point every tool call already used. Phase 3 replaces Workflow's and Pipeline's separate execution paths with one shared, durable, checkpointed Execution Graph Runtime (12 node types), proven to reproduce each existing topology's output byte-for-byte before the migration shipped. Phase 4 adds itemized Session/Working/Entity Memory (alongside the Agent Memory document above, each scoped/TTL'd/Policy-gated) and Document RAG - Knowledge Collections/Sources chunked and embedded on the same Vector Search embeddings path, searched via a `search_knowledge` tool that always cites its source. Phase 5a adds the MCP client role - connect an external MCP server as a Connection, discover its tools via real JSON-RPC, and opt them into the same Tool-Call Firewall with a two-level write gate. Phase 5b adds a visual, free-form drag-and-drop **Agent Teams** canvas (Admin → AI Agent Foundry → Agent Teams) for authoring an Execution Graph directly, with the same Draft → Publish lifecycle and a Runs viewer.
- Team Workspace server: can be exposed on the open internet on an organization's own domain (still self-hosted, never a Lanesra-run SaaS), with opt-in TLS-aware cookies, CORS and always-on security headers.

## Core capabilities

- AI Agent Foundry: named agents with persona, Actions, Memory (with real change history), Skills, guardrails, and delegation, with declarative export/import of an agent or Skill as part of a Solution
- Unified AI Gateway: multi-provider routing (Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible/Gemini/local), automatic failover, token budgets, DLP-triggered air-gapping
- Orchestration: deterministic Pipelines (sequential, consensus, peer-review) with human-in-the-loop approval gates and OTLP tracing, schedule/webhook/workflow-fired runs, a real Evaluation Harness, one unified run history
- Policy Engine & Tool-Call Firewall: six-tier tool risk classification (Read/Low-Write/Write/External-Action/Destructive/Privileged), a workspace/per-agent approval threshold and blocklist, formalized schema→permission→policy→approval→execute→audit dispatch
- Shared Execution Graph Runtime & Agent Teams: a durable, checkpointed 12-node-type graph engine underlying every Workflow and Pipeline, plus a visual drag-and-drop canvas to author one directly
- Memory Architecture & Document RAG: Session/Working/Entity memory (scoped, TTL'd, Policy-gated) via `remember`/`get_memory` tools, and chunked/embedded Knowledge Sources searched via a citation-returning `search_knowledge` tool
- Chat Assistant with real tool access, including an agent context primer (relationship metadata, get_related_records, get_platform_overview)
- Ranked full-text search over Custom Object records (SQLite FTS5, lexical relevance), plus optional semantic (embedding-based) Vector Search via the workspace's own configured provider (desktop only, no bundled vector database)
- Native Model Context Protocol server (`POST /mcp`, JSON-RPC 2.0) & client (connect to an external MCP server and opt its tools in) & a companion CLI, all authenticated with the same scoped API keys / Connection secrets the rest of the product uses
- Admin-defined Custom Objects, Custom Relationships (self-referential hierarchies, polymorphic "any type" targets), custom fields with validation
- Organizations, a materialized-path Organization Unit hierarchy, and Work Teams; a structured Owner (user or team) and Owning Organization Unit on every record, with bulk reassignment and ownership-transfer history
- Business Rules and Workflow Automation across any built-in or custom field, including a related-record condition and a custom-object date-reached trigger
- Screen/App Builder (named layouts by role) and custom Dashboards (KPI/chart/record-list widgets)
- App Builder: publish a named app (a hand-built set of objects, screens and a dashboard) with enforced role/user access
- Companies, contacts, opportunities, products, quotes, orders, invoices, contracts, tasks
- Sales dashboards with admin-configurable KPIs, global search, CSV import/export, PDF print output
- Saved Views (named filter/sort/group-by combinations, reusable as a dashboard data source) and Bulk Actions (update status, reassign owner, tag, archive across a multi-select)
- Industry Data Model: a versioned package manifest format, App Catalog (11 install-ready industry apps), and a Lanesra Industry Foundation package of shared cross-industry objects other packages can depend on (desktop only)
- Deployment Management: Publishers, versioned Solutions, component export/import, update-with-diff
- Integration Hub: encrypted Connections, OpenAPI Connectors, a generic REST API, HMAC-signed Webhooks, CSV data exchange, scheduled Integration Jobs, unified execution logs

## Product principles

- User ownership of business data
- Offline-first desktop direction
- Connected records instead of duplicated free text
- Simplicity before feature volume
- Open-source transparency
- Modern, accessible product design

## Frequently asked

- Is Lanesra OS free and open source? Yes — MIT-licensed, no licence key, no per-seat pricing.
- Can I self-host it instead of a cloud CRM? Yes — desktop runs fully offline on local SQLite; Team Workspace lets a small team share one instance on their own infrastructure.
- Is it just a CRM? No — the same platform underneath the CRM builds any business app, no code, or installs one of 11 ready-made industry apps, and its own AI agents run directly against that data model.
- Does it have a REST API and webhooks? Yes — the Integration Hub's generic REST API, OpenAPI connectors and HMAC-signed webhooks (desktop edition).
- How do I promote customizations from test to production? Deployment Management: curate a named, versioned Solution, export it, import it into another workspace.
- Does it use embeddings or a vector database for AI? By default, no — free-text search over Custom Object records is ranked lexically (SQLite FTS5's `bm25()`). Desktop can optionally reindex records as real embeddings from its own already-configured OpenAI-compatible or Google Gemini provider (Anthropic has no embeddings API) for a second, meaning-based search ranking alongside it - vectors are plain SQLite BLOBs compared by cosine similarity in Rust, not a bundled vector database, and it's opt-in (Admin → LLM & MCP → Vector Search).
